The lesson explains how to weigh dominant purpose, combine tone cues, identify narrator access, collect argument clues, and demonstrate unfair presentation. It also teaches reference matching and paragraph jobs with examples, and shows how each requested sentence family changes interpretation.

Limits include a final request not deciding dominant purpose, dialogue pronouns not deciding narration, classifying only the extract shown, a viewpoint not proving bias, a short passage not needing every detail, nearest nouns not always being references, passive voice not identifying a doer, reported claims not proving truth, and conditions not asserting their fulfillment.
